Subject: FintechCo — post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the team's time. Quick recap of the performance / SLO notes we discussed and proposed next steps (MAP) so we can align on decision criteria. Please confirm or call out items that need correction.

Key SLO targets discussed:
- Latency: p95 < 120ms, p99 target ~350ms for full responses up to 512 tokens; for short responses (<64 tokens) we noted desire for p99 < 200ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 200 req/s, burst to 300 req/s for short windows (~5-10 minutes).
- Concurrency: up to 40 steady concurrent sessions; peaks up to 100 during batch jobs.
- Streaming: client requires token-level streaming (partial responses) for the main UX flow.
- Availability: target 99.9% for inference endpoints.

Proposed immediate MAP items (owners):
1) Performance benchmark run using Redwood harness against a synthetic workload matching your token distribution — owner: Rishi (we'll provide instructions + test account).
2) SLO checklist review and confirm acceptance thresholds — owner: Aisha / FintechCo product.
3) Dedicated capacity recommendation if throughput/concurrency confirmed (pricing impact) — owner: Marissa (I'll share an initial sizing).
4) Security/procurement packet (SOC2, data residency, KMS details) — owner: Neha.

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO checklist template), perf-harness-instructions.md (how to run Redwood perf harness).

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm SLO thresholds: by EOD Tue (2026-02-24)
- Run benchmark: week of 2026-03-02 (can accelerate if you prefer)
- Decide on Dedicated vs Hosted (pricing impact): by 2026-03-12

Would you like to set a 30-minute alignment call early next week to lock thresholds?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side so we can confirm the checklist:
- Latency: For our primary search UX we need p99 < 500ms under peak (we'd prefer < 350ms), and for short chat style replies we'd like p99 < 200ms. The p95/p99 split you listed looks fine.
- Throughput/concurrency: our average traffic is lower (~80-120 req/s) but we have daily peak events that can hit 250-300 req/s and concurrency can spike to ~100 for short windows.
- Streaming: streaming is required for the chat UI (token-by-token). If streaming adds latency for small responses, we may consider server-side aggregation for some endpoints.

Action items for us:
- I'll confirm acceptance thresholds internally by EOD Tue (2026-02-24).
- We will share a small representative dataset (anonymized) and preferred token distribution tomorrow.
- We need the perf harness + test account details so our infra team can run the benchmark — can Rishi coordinate?

Also, procurement will start a security questionnaire — Neha, can you share SOC2 certs and any info on data retention?

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product
FintechCo
